This site collects the essentials from Posit's official cheatsheets into a
single, browsable reference — from finding your way around the RStudio IDE
to importing, wrangling, and visualizing data with the tidyverse.

::: {.callout-tip}
## New to R?
Start with [RStudio IDE](rstudio-ide.qmd) to get oriented, then move to
[Importing Data](data-import.qmd) and [Transforming Data](data-transformation.qmd)
to start working with your own data sets.
:::

## Why the tidyverse?

Every reference on this site centers on the **tidyverse**, a collection of R
packages designed to work together around a shared philosophy: data should
be *tidy* — each variable in its own column, each observation in its own row
— and functions should be predictable, pipeable, and human-readable.

`readr` — import
· `dplyr` — transform
· `stringr` — text
· `forcats` — factors
· `ggplot2` — visualize
· `RStudio` — workbench

## A typical R workflow

1. **Set up your project.** Open RStudio, create a Project (`File > New Project`), and organize your scripts, data, and outputs. See [RStudio IDE](rstudio-ide.qmd).
2. **Import your data.** Read CSVs, Excel files, or Google Sheets into tibbles with `read_csv()`, `read_excel()`, or `read_sheet()`. See [Importing Data](data-import.qmd).
3. **Clean and reshape it.** Filter rows, select columns, create new variables, and summarize groups with dplyr verbs. See [Transforming Data](data-transformation.qmd).
4. **Wrangle text and categories.** Clean up messy text with stringr and tame categorical variables with forcats. See [Strings](strings.qmd) and [Factors](factors.qmd).
5. **Visualize and share.** Build layered plots with ggplot2, then knit results into a report with R Markdown or Quarto. See [Data Visualization](data-visualization.qmd).
